# #3667: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 42899386056](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42899386056) on `staging` (`4327b2b`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [e2e component (chrome)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42899386056/job/130161274898) | failure |
| [e2e (2/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42899386056/job/130161275908) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `staging`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`, and you take it before every other queued item): production promotes itself only from a daily run on `staging` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix. The fix lands on `main` like any other, and promote-staging.yml brings it to `staging` within two hours; the next daily run there that passes promotes it, or a `/promote` on the production issue tests staging's newer commit sooner. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

3. Reproduce the component job: `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` (only prerequisite; the component dev server compiles `apps/web/src` itself on port 5273), then `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome`. - [ ] The failing spec(s) in shard 2/8 and in the component run are identified from reproduction output, not guessed.
- [ ] Each is fixed by hardening (no `skip`/`only`/quarantine, no lowered bar, no raised timeout as the fix) or by a product-bug fix with its own unit test.

- [ ] No file under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, or `bot/` is changed; no unrelated code is reformatted.

## Risks

- Each shard boots its own server and R144 reseeds at boot; specs 10, 44, and 45 share fixture accounts (`e2e-econ`, invite codes), so never run shard 2 against a server another shard or a stale run is using, and do not add retries (the shard action deliberately leaves Cypress retries at config value).

- The client never enforces rules and never sees hidden information (rule 7): a spec failure showing hidden state or client-side rule enforcement is a product bug, not a spec bug.
- `cargo test` rewrites `apps/web/src/wire/`; commit any diff it produces. `main` moved 10 commits past the tested staging commit, so confirm the failure reproduces on this base before editing.
- If the root cause lands in `crates/engine` or `crates/ai`, stop and re-rate hard: this plan's medium rating no longer holds.

## Open questions

- The job logs were unreachable from here (no GitHub credential), so the suspects in step 3–5 are investigation order, not diagnosed causes; the reproduction output decides.
- If reproduction on this base passes (a later `main` commit already fixed it), do not invent a change: report which commit fixed it and ask a person to run `gh workflow run super.yml --ref bot/issue-3667` to confirm, since the bot cannot dispatch runs.
- If any part of the fix must live in `.github/` (runner, matrix, shard count, artifact plumbing), give the exact lines and ask a person to make that part; land everything else from this plan.

Comment by @jgoetzmann at 2026-11-11T02:59:08Z:

Root causes for the two red jobs, from the logs of super run 42899386056 (attempt 2):

- **`e2e (2/8)`:** only `45-economy-loop.cy.ts`, and it never compiles: `Webpack Compilation Error … UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from "node:fs" is not handled by plugins` (and `node:path`, `node:url`). The cause is #3529: `apps/web/src/wire/cards.ts` now imports `PATCH_VERSION` from `#jackioh-patch-meta`.
  - Every Vite pipeline resolves that through `patchMeta()`: vite build/dev, vitest, and the component specs via `e2e/cypress.config.ts`'s `component.devServer`.
  - Cypress **e2e** specs are bundled by Cypress's default webpack preprocessor, which has no such plugin. It falls back to `apps/web/package.json`'s `imports` map, `./patch-meta.ts`, which reads `patches.json` with `node:fs`.
  - Spec 45 reaches `wire/cards.ts` through `apps/web/src/cards/versions.ts`, then `cards/art/pictures.ts`.
  - The production bundle (Vite) is unaffected.
  - Possible fixes:
    - give the e2e preprocessor a resolution for `#jackioh-patch-meta`;
    - or a `browser` condition in `apps/web/package.json`'s `imports` that webpack honours and Vite's plugin pre-empts;
    - or keep spec 45 off `wire/cards.ts`.
  - Verify with `cd e2e && pnpm exec cypress run --spec cypress/e2e/45-economy-loop.cy.ts`, against the server and the client as e2e/README.md says.
- **`e2e component (chrome)`:** only `fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx` (3 of 4 tests), the phone frame budget. That is #3674's work, already planned as hard; build on it rather than redo it here.
